title: Luke Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 2.

questions.question: In Luke 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The shepherds abiding in the field
Mary brought forth her firstborn son
questions.correctAnswer: A decree from Caesar Augustus
questions.explanation: This event is described in Luke 2:1, where it states that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus.

questions.question: Who was governor of Syria when the taxing was first made?
questions.correctAnswer: Cyrenius
questions.explanation: Luke 2:2 mentions that this taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.

questions.question: To which city did Joseph go to be taxed?
questions.correctAnswer: Bethlehem
questions.explanation: In Luke 2:4, it states that Joseph went to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem.

questions.question: Why did Joseph go to Bethlehem?
questions.correctAnswer: To be taxed
questions.explanation: Luke 2:5 states that Joseph went to be taxed with Mary, his espoused wife.

questions.question: What did Mary wrap her firstborn son in?
questions.correctAnswer: Swaddling clothes
questions.explanation: Luke 2:7 indicates that she wrapped him in swaddling clothes.

questions.question: Where was the baby laid after his birth?
questions.correctAnswer: In a manger
questions.explanation: According to Luke 2:7, the baby was laid in a manger because there was no room for them in the inn.

questions.question: What were the shepherds doing in the field?
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping watch over their flock
questions.explanation: Luke 2:8 states that the shepherds were abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.

questions.question: What did the angel say to the shepherds?
questions.correctAnswer: Do not be afraid
questions.explanation: In Luke 2:10, the angel said unto them, 'Fear not'.

questions.question: What sign was given to the shepherds?
options: A babe wrapped in swaddling clothes
questions.correctAnswer: A babe wrapped in swaddling clothes
questions.explanation: Luke 2:12 states that the sign unto them was the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger.

questions.question: What did the heavenly host say?
options: Glory to God in the highest
questions.correctAnswer: Glory to God in the highest
questions.explanation: According to Luke 2:14, the heavenly host praised God saying, 'Glory to God in the highest'.

questions.question: What did the shepherds decide to do after hearing the angels?
questions.correctAnswer: Go to Bethlehem
questions.explanation: Luke 2:15 indicates that the shepherds said to one another, 'Let us now go even unto Bethlehem'.

questions.question: Did the shepherds find Mary, Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 2:16 confirms that they came with haste and found Mary, Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger.

questions.question: Did the shepherds make known abroad the saying concerning the child?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In Luke 2:17, it states that when they had seen it, they made known abroad the saying concerning the child.

questions.question: The text says that all who heard the shepherds wondered at the things told by the shepherds.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not state that all who heard it wondered; it only mentions those who heard it in general terms without specifying 'all'.

questions.question: The angel of the Lord came to the shepherds while they were in the city.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The angel came to the shepherds while they were abiding in the field, not in the city as stated in Luke 2:8.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Mary do with all the things that were told to her?
options: She kept them and pondered them in her heart.
questions.correctAnswer: She kept them and pondered them in her heart.
questions.explanation: Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart. (Luke 2:19)

questions.question: What does Luke 2:20 promise will happen if someone praises God for what they have heard and seen?
options: They will be filled with joy.
They will return home glorifying God.
They will find favor with men.
questions.correctAnswer: They will return home glorifying God.
questions.explanation: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, as it was told unto them. (Luke 2:20)

questions.question: What was the name given to the child on the eighth day?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus
questions.explanation: His name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb. (Luke 2:21)

questions.question: What does Luke 2:22 describe as being accomplished before bringing Jesus to the temple?
options: The days of her purification according to the law.
questions.correctAnswer: The days of her purification according to the law.
questions.explanation: When the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem. (Luke 2:22)

questions.question: According to Luke 2:23, who shall be called holy to the Lord?
options: Every female that opens the womb.
Every male that opens the womb.
questions.correctAnswer: Every male that opens the womb.
questions.explanation: Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord. (Luke 2:23)

questions.question: What type of sacrifice did they offer according to the law of the Lord?
options: A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
questions.correctAnswer: A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
questions.explanation: To offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons. (Luke 2:24)

questions.question: What does Luke 2:25 say about Simeon?
options: He was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel.
He was a teacher in the temple.
questions.correctAnswer: He was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel.
questions.explanation: There was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel. (Luke 2:25)

questions.question: What was revealed to Simeon by the Holy Ghost?
options: He would see the temple destroyed.
He would not see death before seeing the Lord's Christ.
questions.correctAnswer: He would not see death before seeing the Lord's Christ.
questions.explanation: It was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ. (Luke 2:26)

questions.question: What happened when Simeon saw Jesus in the temple?
options: He took Jesus up in his arms and blessed God.
questions.correctAnswer: He took Jesus up in his arms and blessed God.
questions.explanation: Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said. (Luke 2:28)

questions.question: What did Simeon declare about seeing God's salvation?
options: It was only for the Jews.
He had seen it according to God's word.
questions.correctAnswer: He had seen it according to God's word.
questions.explanation: Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: For mine eyes have seen thy salvation. (Luke 2:29-30)

questions.question: Simeon described Jesus as a light for whom?
options: The Gentiles and the glory of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: The Gentiles and the glory of Israel.
questions.explanation: A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. (Luke 2:32)

questions.question: What did Simeon say would happen to many in Israel because of Jesus?
options: They would fall and rise again.
questions.correctAnswer: They would fall and rise again.
questions.explanation: This child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel. (Luke 2:34)

questions.question: True or False: Mary was told by Simeon that a sword would pierce through her soul.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: A sword shall pierce through thy own soul also. (Luke 2:35)

questions.question: True or False: Anna was a young virgin who had just married.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Anna was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity. (Luke 2:36)

questions.question: True or False: The shepherds were afraid when the angel appeared to them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The shepherds were sore afraid when the angel of the Lord came upon them. (Luke 2:9)

hard.title: Luke Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 2.

questions.question: How long was Anna a widow, according to Luke 2:37?
questions.correctAnswer: About fourscore and four years
questions.explanation: Luke 2:37 states that Anna was 'a widow of about fourscore and four years.'

questions.question: What two spiritual disciplines did Anna practice night and day as described in Luke 2:37?
questions.correctAnswer: Fastings and prayers
questions.explanation: Luke 2:37 says Anna 'departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.'

questions.question: What was Anna’s response when she saw Jesus in the temple, according to Luke 2:38?
options: She gave thanks to the Lord and spoke of Him to all who looked for redemption in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: She gave thanks to the Lord and spoke of Him to all who looked for redemption in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Luke 2:38 states that Anna 'gave thanks likewise unto the Lord, and spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem.'

questions.question: After fulfilling all things according to the law, where did Joseph and Mary return with Jesus, as per Luke 2:39?
options: Galilee, to their own city Nazareth
questions.correctAnswer: Galilee, to their own city Nazareth
questions.explanation: Luke 2:39 states they 'returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth' after fulfilling the law.

questions.question: At what age did Jesus stay behind in Jerusalem when his parents began their journey home, according to Luke 2:43?
questions.correctAnswer: Twelve years old
questions.explanation: Luke 2:42-43 describe Jesus being twelve years old when he tarried behind in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'waxes strong' (Greek: 'ἐνδυναμοῦται') in Luke 2:40 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Grows powerful or strengthens
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'ἐνδυναμοῦται' from Luke 2:40 means to become strong or powerful, indicating Jesus’ spiritual and physical growth.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Luke 2:14, 'Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men'?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Luke 2:14 uses parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, balancing 'Glory to God in the highest' with 'peace on earth' to emphasize praise and peace.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of Jesus being a light to the Gentiles as mentioned in Luke 2:32?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 42:6
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:6 prophesies a servant who will be 'a light to the Gentiles,' directly connecting to Luke 2:32's description of Jesus.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of Jesus increasing in wisdom and stature from Luke 2:52?
questions.correctAnswer: Ephesians 4:15
questions.explanation: Ephesians 4:15 speaks of 'growing up in all things into him, which is the head, even Christ,' echoing Jesus’ growth in wisdom and favor in Luke 2:52.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus being found in the temple discussing with doctors in Luke 2:46?
options: Joseph and Mary searching for three days
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph and Mary searching for three days
questions.explanation: Luke 2:45 states that after not finding Jesus, they turned back to Jerusalem seeking him, leading directly to Luke 2:46 where they find him in the temple.

questions.question: What typological significance does Simeon’s blessing in Luke 2:34-35 have in relation to the Old Testament?
options: Foreshadows the suffering servant motif of Isaiah
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadows the suffering servant motif of Isaiah
questions.explanation: Simeon’s words in Luke 2:34-35, especially the sword piercing Mary’s soul, foreshadow the suffering servant described in Isaiah 53.

questions.question: How does Luke 2:40 reflect the concept of 'grace' from the Greek word 'χάρις' used in the New Testament?
options: It indicates divine favor and empowerment
questions.correctAnswer: It indicates divine favor and empowerment
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'χάρις' (grace) in Luke 2:40 signifies God's unmerited favor, empowering Jesus in wisdom and spirit, consistent with Pauline theology.

questions.question: Which literary structure is evident in Luke 2:41-52 focusing on Jesus’ growth and his temple experience?
options: Chiasm with center on the temple discussion
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm with center on the temple discussion
questions.explanation: Luke 2:41-52 presents a chiasm with the central focus on Jesus discussing with the doctors in the temple (v.46-47), framed by his yearly visits and growth.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 2:49, Jesus was unaware that his parents were seeking him because he was about his Father's business.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 2:49 shows Jesus questioning why they sought him, indicating he was focused on his Father's work, unaware of their sorrow.

questions.question: True or False: Luke 2:50 states that Joseph and Mary clearly understood the meaning of Jesus’ words about being about his Father's business.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 2:50 explicitly says 'they understood not the saying which he spake unto them,' showing their lack of understanding.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 2:7 teach about salvation?
options: The omnipotence of God in creation
questions.correctAnswer: The humility of Christ's incarnation
questions.explanation: Luke 2:7 describes Jesus being born and laid in a manger because there was no room at the inn, illustrating the humble circumstances of the incarnation, key to understanding salvation's humility.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 2:21 teach about Christ's identity?
options: The preordained name Jesus as Savior
The divinity of the Holy Spirit
The rejection of the Messiah by Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The preordained name Jesus as Savior
questions.explanation: Luke 2:21 states the child was named Jesus as the angel commanded before conception, emphasizing Jesus' identity as the divinely appointed Savior.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 2:35 teach about the suffering of Christ and its spiritual significance?
options: Christ's suffering reveals the thoughts of many hearts
Christ's suffering is purely physical without spiritual effect
Christ avoids all suffering by divine intervention
Christ's suffering is unrelated to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's suffering reveals the thoughts of many hearts
questions.explanation: Luke 2:35 describes a sword piercing Mary’s soul and the child being set for the fall and rising of many, indicating the salvific and revelatory nature of Christ’s suffering.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 2:26 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Luke 2:26 shows that the Holy Ghost revealed to Simeon that he would not die before seeing the Messiah, reflecting God's omniscience in foreknowledge.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 2:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Peacefulness
questions.explanation: Luke 2:14 proclaims 'Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men,' demonstrating God's attribute of peace.

questions.question: How does Luke 2:9-11 connect to the theme of divine revelation in the Old Testament?
options: It shows the angel announcing the birth of the Messiah to lowly shepherds, fulfilling prophecies of God revealing salvation to the humble.
It denies any connection to Old Testament prophecy.
It reveals a new god unrelated to Yahweh.
It emphasizes human efforts rather than divine initiative.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the angel announcing the birth of the Messiah to lowly shepherds, fulfilling prophecies of God revealing salvation to the humble.
questions.explanation: Luke 2:9-11 depicts the angel announcing Jesus’ birth to shepherds, fulfilling Old Testament themes like Isaiah 61:1 where God reveals salvation to the humble and oppressed.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Luke 2:22-24 have with Old Testament covenantal law?
options: It demonstrates Jesus' family's fidelity to Mosaic Law by presenting Him in the temple and offering the prescribed sacrifice.
It rejects the necessity of the Law for salvation.
It introduces a new law abolishing previous ordinances.
It focuses on pagan rituals unrelated to Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates Jesus' family's fidelity to Mosaic Law by presenting Him in the temple and offering the prescribed sacrifice.
questions.explanation: Luke 2:22-24 shows Jesus’ presentation in the temple and offering according to Levitical law, connecting Jesus to the covenantal promises of Israel.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Luke 2:40 and Luke 2:52 teach about the nature of Christ's humanity and sanctification?
options: Christ's growth in wisdom, strength, and favor reflects true human development and divine grace.
Christ was omniscient from birth, needing no growth.
Christ's humanity is merely a disguise without real human traits.
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's growth in wisdom, strength, and favor reflects true human development and divine grace.
questions.explanation: Luke 2:40 and 2:52 together affirm Jesus' genuine humanity growing physically, intellectually, and spiritually, sustained by God's grace.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Luke 2:29-32 and Luke 2:34-35 teach about Christ's salvific role and suffering?
options: Christ is the salvation prepared for all people, but also a sign of division and suffering.
Christ is only a political leader without spiritual significance.
Christ’s role is limited to Israel with no universal impact.
Christ avoids suffering and is only a triumphant king.
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is the salvation prepared for all people, but also a sign of division and suffering.
questions.explanation: Verses 29-32 show Simeon recognizing Christ as salvation for all, while 34-35 warn of opposition and suffering, highlighting the dual nature of Christ’s mission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Luke 2:19 and Luke 2:51 teach about Mary’s role in the incarnation and sanctification?
options: Mary’s contemplative keeping of Jesus’ words signifies her unique participation in God’s redemptive plan.
Mary is portrayed as divine herself.
Mary rejects the significance of Jesus’ mission.
Mary’s role is purely biological with no spiritual dimension.
questions.correctAnswer: Mary’s contemplative keeping of Jesus’ words signifies her unique participation in God’s redemptive plan.
questions.explanation: Luke 2:19 and 2:51 emphasize Mary pondering and treasuring Jesus’ words, reflecting her faithful and contemplative role in salvation history.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the nativity narrative in Luke 2:8-20 is a myth created to glorify Jesus. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It depicts a genuine divine revelation to humble shepherds, emphasizing God's initiative in revealing salvation to the lowly.
It confirms Jesus as a mythological figure unrelated to history.
It shows an attempt to fabricate a royal lineage for Jesus.
It suggests angels only appeared symbolically and not historically.
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts a genuine divine revelation to humble shepherds, emphasizing God's initiative in revealing salvation to the lowly.
questions.explanation: Luke 2:8-20 describes an angelic announcement to shepherds as a real event highlighting God's sovereign choice to reveal the Messiah to the marginalized, supporting historicity and theological truth.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 2:25 teach about the role of the Holy Spirit in salvation history?
options: The Holy Spirit guides and reveals messianic truth to the devout.
The Holy Spirit is irrelevant to Old Testament saints.
The Holy Spirit only acts after Pentecost.
The Holy Spirit is a created angelic being.
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit guides and reveals messianic truth to the devout.
questions.explanation: Luke 2:25 shows Simeon as just and devout with the Holy Ghost upon him, indicating the Spirit’s active role in revealing salvation even before Christ’s public ministry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 2:1 demonstrate in the context of the census decreed by Caesar Augustus?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Luke 2:1 situates Jesus’ birth during Caesar Augustus’ decree, showing God's sovereignty over human history and rulers to fulfill divine purposes.

questions.question: How does Luke 2:15-18 contribute to the narrative arc of divine revelation to the marginalized?
options: It shows shepherds, socially lowly figures, as the first recipients and proclaimers of the Messiah’s birth.
It depicts kings as the primary receivers of revelation.
It denies any divine communication to common people.
It emphasizes secret revelation only to priests.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows shepherds, socially lowly figures, as the first recipients and proclaimers of the Messiah’s birth.
questions.explanation: Luke 2:15-18 narrates shepherds going quickly to see Jesus and spreading the news, highlighting God’s pattern of revealing salvation to the humble and marginalized.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Luke 2:41-47 teach about Christ’s early understanding of His divine mission?
options: Jesus at twelve was aware of His unique relationship with the Father and prioritized divine business over familial concerns.
Jesus was unaware of His divine mission until adulthood.
Jesus rejected His divine calling at a young age.
Jesus was solely focused on earthly matters.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus at twelve was aware of His unique relationship with the Father and prioritized divine business over familial concerns.
questions.explanation: Luke 2:41-47 shows Jesus staying behind in the temple, astonishing teachers with His understanding, and stating He must be about His Father’s business, evidencing early divine self-awareness.
